neighbours.label: the head of a noun phrase naming a quantity to be found or measured (the amount, the proportion, the angle, the values of)
fire: To solve the system, we first find the values of x and y.
The gauge reflects the amount of fuel left in the tank.
The survey estimates the proportion of adults who smoke daily.
Measure the angle that the beam makes with the floor.
Mobility is a measure of the tendency of a chemical to move through soil.
The chart shows the percentage of students who passed the exam.
Engineers calculated the rate at which heat escapes through the wall.
The ratio describes the fraction of light that reaches the sensor.
quiet: To solve the puzzle, we first open the box on the table.
The gauge sits next to the door of the fuel tank.
The survey was mailed to adults who live in the city.
Paint the beam that runs along the floor.
Mobility is a feature of the new chairs in the waiting room.
The chart hangs on the wall of the classroom near the exam desk.
Engineers painted the wall through which the pipes run.
The lens sits in front of the sensor inside the camera.

notes: Card peaks: 'find the' (values of), 'the amount of', 'the propensity of', 'the proportion of', 'the angle that'. Near misses keep 'the' + concrete, non-quantity nouns.
